entities.name: PMID:25450500
observations: Lowe et al. (2015) tested cumulative changes to guinea-pig ovalbumin sensitisation and inhalation-challenge protocols after loss of late asthmatic response (LAR), airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR), early asthmatic response (EAR), and inflammatory-cell responses.

Increasing ovalbumin challenge from 100 to 300 μg/ml restored AHR and eosinophils and increased the EAR peak; increasing sensitisation from 100 to 150 μg increased total cells, especially eosinophils.
Increasing aluminium hydroxide or extending the sensitisation-to-challenge interval from 15 to 21 days revealed a LAR and increased lymphocytes and eosinophils.
The authors concluded that declining allergic responses could be restored by increasing sensitisation and challenge conditions, while noting dissociation among EAR, LAR, AHR, and inflammation.
